paragraphs.title: Solomon’s Wives and the Turning of His Heart

easy.explanation: The passage says Solomon loved many strange, or foreign, women.
easy.q: What kind of women did Solomon love?

easy.explanation: First Kings 11:3 says Solomon had seven hundred wives, princesses.
easy.q: How many wives did Solomon have?

easy.explanation: The passage repeatedly says that his wives turned away his heart.
easy.q: What did Solomon’s wives do to his heart?

answers: They turned his heart after other gods
medium.explanation: The women turned Solomon’s heart after their gods.
medium.q: What happened because Solomon loved foreign women?

answers: Women in a secondary marital status
medium.explanation: The passage distinguishes Solomon’s wives from his three hundred concubines.
medium.q: What does the KJV word “concubines” refer to in this passage?

answers: He built high places where they could worship
medium.explanation: Solomon built high places for the gods of his foreign wives.
medium.q: What did Solomon do for the gods of his foreign wives?

answers: He did not remain fully faithful and followed other gods
He did not reign forty years
challenge.explanation: His heart was turned toward other gods instead of remaining wholly faithful to the Lord.
challenge.q: Why was Solomon’s heart said not to be perfect with the Lord?

answers: The Lord had appeared to him twice and commanded him not to follow other gods
He had never heard the Lord’s commands
challenge.explanation: The Lord had appeared to Solomon twice and had specifically commanded him concerning this matter.
challenge.q: What made Solomon’s sin especially serious?

answers: His wives caused him to leave Jerusalem
His wives stopped him from building
His wives turned his heart, and he built places of worship for their gods
challenge.explanation: The passage connects Solomon’s many foreign wives with his turning heart and his building of high places.
challenge.q: What connection does the passage make between Solomon’s wives and idolatry?

paragraphs.title: The Decree to Divide the Kingdom

easy.explanation: The Lord said, “I will surely rend the kingdom from thee.”
easy.q: What did the Lord say He would do to the kingdom?

answers: During the reign of his son
easy.explanation: The Lord said He would rend it out of the hand of Solomon’s son.
easy.q: When would the kingdom be divided?

easy.explanation: The Lord promised to give one tribe to Solomon’s son.
easy.q: How much of the kingdom would remain with David’s house?

answers: Solomon had not kept the Lord’s covenant and statutes
medium.explanation: The decree came because Solomon had not kept the Lord’s covenant and statutes.
medium.q: Why was the kingdom to be divided?

answers: Divide the kingdom and its rule
medium.explanation: To rend the kingdom means to tear away and divide its authority.
medium.q: What does “rend the kingdom” mean here?

medium.explanation: The Lord said the division would not happen during Solomon’s days.
medium.q: What did the Lord delay until Solomon’s son’s time?

challenge.explanation: The Lord mentioned David and Jerusalem as reasons for preserving one tribe.
challenge.q: What two reasons are given for leaving one tribe with David’s house?

answers: The judgment was certain, but would not happen immediately
The kingdom would never be divided
challenge.explanation: The division was decreed, but its execution was delayed until the next generation.
challenge.q: What can be learned from delaying the judgment until Solomon’s son?

answers: Solomon would rule all the land, but Jerusalem would be destroyed
Jerusalem would remain, but David would be forgotten
The kingdom would be divided, yet part would remain with David’s house
challenge.explanation: Although the kingdom would be torn away, one tribe would remain with David’s house.
challenge.q: What is the main contrast in the decree?

paragraphs.title: Hadad the Edomite and Rezon the Aramean

easy.explanation: The passage calls him Hadad the Edomite.
Hadad fled with certain Edomites to Egypt while he was still a little child.
easy.q: Where did Hadad flee as a child?

easy.explanation: Rezon and his men came to Damascus and reigned there.

answers: The Lord stirred him up as an adversary, and he returned toward his own country
medium.explanation: The Lord raised Hadad as an adversary against Solomon.
medium.q: Why was Hadad an enemy of Solomon?

answers: A prophet who warned the king
A servant in the royal house
medium.explanation: Hadad and Rezon are presented as enemies who opposed Israel.
medium.q: What does “adversary” mean in this passage?

answers: He gathered men, came to Damascus, and reigned there
medium.explanation: Rezon gathered a band, went to Damascus, and became its ruler.
medium.q: How did Rezon become ruler in Damascus?

answers: Edom, Egypt, and a desire to return to his country
challenge.explanation: Hadad fled from Edom to Egypt and later asked to return to his own country.
challenge.q: Which sequence correctly describes Hadad’s journey?

answers: They were both descendants of David
They both became enemies or sources of trouble for Israel during Solomon’s reign
challenge.explanation: Both men are described as adversaries who troubled Solomon and Israel.
challenge.q: What did Hadad and Rezon have in common?

answers: Pharaoh gave him a house, food, land, and a wife
challenge.explanation: Pharaoh welcomed Hadad and provided for him in several ways.
challenge.q: What does the passage emphasize about Hadad’s relationship with Pharaoh?

paragraphs.title: Jeroboam Rises and Challenges the King

easy.explanation: Jeroboam is described as an Ephrathite of the house of Joseph.
easy.q: From which family or tribe was Jeroboam?

answers: Ruler over all the charge of the house of Joseph
easy.explanation: Solomon made him ruler over all the charge of the house of Joseph.
easy.q: What position did Solomon give Jeroboam?

easy.explanation: The prophet Ahijah the Shilonite found Jeroboam in the way.
easy.q: Who met Jeroboam on the way?

answers: Solomon built Millo and repaired the breaches of the city of David
medium.explanation: The passage identifies Solomon’s work on Millo and the city’s breaches as the cause.
medium.q: What was connected with Jeroboam’s lifting his hand against the king?

medium.explanation: The phrase presents Jeroboam as a capable and energetic man.
medium.q: What does the KJV phrase “mighty man of valour” suggest about Jeroboam?

answers: He rent it into twelve pieces
medium.explanation: Ahijah caught the new garment and rent it into twelve pieces.
medium.q: What did Ahijah do with the new garment?

answers: He was a capable man given an important responsibility, so he had influence to oppose the king
He was a foreign king outside Solomon’s authority
He was a prophet who did not serve in government
challenge.explanation: Jeroboam was capable and had been placed over the charge of Joseph’s house before opposing Solomon.
challenge.q: How did Jeroboam’s position relate to his challenge against Solomon?

answers: It emphasizes that the meeting and prophetic sign occurred without others present
It shows that Jeroboam had escaped from Egypt
It describes the construction of Millo
challenge.explanation: The detail highlights the private setting of the prophetic meeting.
challenge.q: Why does the passage mention that Ahijah and Jeroboam were alone in the field?

answers: The tearing or division of the kingdom
challenge.explanation: The torn garment symbolized the coming division of the kingdom.
challenge.q: What did the tearing of the garment represent?

easy.explanation: Ahijah said the Lord would give ten tribes to Jeroboam.
easy.q: How many tribes would Jeroboam receive?

easy.explanation: One tribe would remain with David’s house.

answers: He had to build high places for other gods
He had to keep the Lord’s commands and walk in His ways
easy.explanation: The promise depended on Jeroboam’s obedience to the Lord.
easy.q: What was required of Jeroboam to receive a lasting house?

answers: The people forsook the Lord and worshipped other gods
medium.explanation: The prophecy cites Israel’s forsaking the Lord and worshipping idols.
medium.q: What reason for the division of the kingdom is given in Ahijah’s prophecy?

answers: A continuing line or surviving house
medium.explanation: The image of a light refers to the continuing presence of David’s house.
medium.q: What does the word “light” suggest in the promise concerning David?

answers: That he would receive a sure house like David’s
That he would possess Jerusalem only
medium.explanation: The Lord promised to build Jeroboam a sure house if he walked in His ways.
medium.q: What did the Lord promise Jeroboam if he obeyed His commands?

answers: The kingdom was torn from Solomon and the ten tribes were given to Jeroboam
Jeroboam was sent to defend Solomon
Solomon received the ten tribes from Jeroboam
challenge.explanation: The prophecy explains that Jeroboam would receive the ten tribes taken from Solomon’s rule.
challenge.q: How does the prophecy connect Solomon’s judgment with Jeroboam’s rise?

answers: For David’s sake and for Jerusalem’s sake
Because Jeroboam refused to take it
challenge.explanation: The prophecy specifically names David and Jerusalem as the reasons.
challenge.q: Why would one tribe remain with David’s house?

answers: He had to continue worshipping idols
He had to stay away from Israel
He had to hearken to the Lord and do what was right in His sight
challenge.explanation: Jeroboam’s promise was conditional on hearing the Lord’s commands and walking in His ways.
challenge.q: What moral condition accompanied the promise of kingship to Jeroboam?

paragraphs.title: Jeroboam’s Flight and the End of Solomon’s Reign

easy.explanation: The passage says Solomon sought to kill Jeroboam.
easy.q: Why did Jeroboam flee from Solomon?

easy.explanation: Jeroboam fled into Egypt to Shishak king of Egypt.
The passage records that Solomon reigned for forty years.
easy.q: How long did Solomon reign in Jerusalem?

medium.explanation: Jeroboam stayed in Egypt until Solomon’s death.
medium.q: How long did Jeroboam remain in Egypt?

answers: In the book of the acts of Solomon
In the book of the kings of Egypt
In the book of the wars of David
medium.explanation: The passage refers readers to the book of the acts of Solomon.
medium.q: Where were the rest of Solomon’s acts recorded?

medium.explanation: Rehoboam, Solomon’s son, reigned in his stead.

answers: It ended after forty years, followed by his death and Rehoboam’s succession
It continued after Rehoboam became king
It ended when Solomon moved to Egypt
challenge.explanation: The passage records Solomon’s forty-year reign, death, burial, and succession by Rehoboam.
challenge.q: What does the closing section show about Solomon’s reign?

answers: It shows that he accepted Solomon’s rule permanently
It shows that Solomon’s opposition forced the future rival king into exile
It shows that Jeroboam became Pharaoh
challenge.explanation: Jeroboam escaped Solomon’s attempt to kill him and remained in Egypt until Solomon died.
challenge.q: What is the significance of Jeroboam’s flight to Egypt?

answers: Solomon sought Jeroboam’s death, Jeroboam fled, Solomon died, and Rehoboam reigned
Rehoboam fled, Solomon died, and Jeroboam became king immediately
Jeroboam killed Solomon, then returned from Egypt and ruled Jerusalem
challenge.explanation: These events occur in that order in the closing verses.
challenge.q: Which sequence best summarizes the end of the chapter?
